stories.excerpt: U.S. Senate race in Mississippi remained too close to call Wednesday, with Democratic challenger Scott Colom leading Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by just 43 votes out of more than 900,000 cast, even as Democrats secured control of the chamber. With nearly all precincts reporting, each candidate held 48.9 percent of the vote. About 97 percent of the vote had been counted. The Associated Press had not called the race as of Wednesday morning Eastern time. Mississippi has not elected a Democrat statewide in more than 40 years. Nadal won 22 Grand Slam titles, two Olympic gold medals and helped Spain claim five Davis Cups before retiring in 2024. Real's members will be asked to approve the 40-year-old's appointment to the board at a meeting later this month. stories.title: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations
stories.description: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.
stories.excerpt: Needles and other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets handed out over Halloween in Germany, Austria and Hungary, prompting police to issue warnings to parents to check what their children have been given. Police in a number of German states have reported cases, from Bavaria in the south-east to Lower Saxony in the north. A girl aged nine hurt her tongue while eating a chocolate bar in Bremervörde, west of Hamburg. A 5cm-long (2in) pin was then found inside it. Meanwhile, police in Hungary have launched a criminal investigation after nails, screws and pieces of wire were found in sweets handed out to children who had been trick-or-treating in and around the town of Gyömrő, to the east of Budapest. The local authority said one young girl had been handed a toffee with a nail inside a chocolate wrapper and that she had fortunately noticed in time and had not swallowed the sweet. stories.title: Ruto: Kenya must produce more than it consumes and sell more of what it makes
stories.description: Kenya’s next big test: Can local factories replace imports and win Africa’s markets?
stories.excerpt: Kenya, November 04, 2026 - President William Ruto says Kenya should stop depending so much on goods made elsewhere. Speaking at the Kenya Industrialisation Summit in Nairobi on November 4, 2026, he said the country should make more of what it uses and sell more of what it makes. His message was simple: a rich country is not known by what it buys, but by what it can produce. He wants more Kenyan factories, more local materials and more Kenyan goods sold across Africa. This idea is called industrialisation. It means building industries that turn raw materials into finished goods. For example, instead of exporting raw hides, Kenya could make leather shoes. Instead of importing furniture, local carpenters and factories could supply homes, schools and offices. Ruto pointed to housing as one example. stories.excerpt: For decades, Texas Democrats have dreamt of turning the state blue, rallying around exciting candidates who drew big crowds and big money but could not ultimately overcome the state’s stubborn conservative majority.
